name: DarkFactory
description: A modular, Postgres-first, AI-native application foundation.
description_good_justification: README opening description (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md) and package metadata (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) describe the domain-neutral, Postgres-first application foundation.
interact_justification: README setup/use (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md), SUPPORT (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/SUPPORT.md), and CONTRIBUTING (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONTRIBUTING.md) explain obtaining, using, reporting on, and contributing to the software.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains issue-first cases, focused branches, pull requests, review evidence, and acceptance flow.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING requirements (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONTRIBUTING.md) links the architecture and conventions and requires tests, documentation, generated-artifact checks, and scoped verification.
floss_license_justification: The delivered repository is MIT-licensed in the root LICENSE (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/LICENSE) and declares MIT in package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json).
floss_license_osi_justification: The root LICENSE (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/LICENSE) is the standard MIT license, an OSI-approved license.
license_location_justification: The license is in the standard top-level LICENSE (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/LICENSE) file.
documentation_basics_justification: Installation, startup, use, and secure-use guidance are in the README (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md), local-development guide (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/local-development.md), and security guide (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/security.md).
documentation_interface_justification: External routes are summarized in the README (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md); the API contract is the generated OpenAPI 3.1 document (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/api/openapi.json).
sites_https_justification: The homepage, repository, issue tracker, and planned release are all under the HTTPS GitHub repository (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory) origin.
discussion_justification: Public, searchable, URL-addressable discussion is available through GitHub issues (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues) and pull requests (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/pulls).
english_justification: The README (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md), policies, issue forms, source comments, and contribution process are in English.
maintained_justification: The public main-branch history (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/commits/main) and active CI workflow (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/actions/workflows/ci.yml) show current maintenance. Limitation: Maintenance is a current-state assertion and must be changed if the project becomes inactive.
repo_public_justification: The GitHub repository (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory) is publicly readable and reports main as its default branch.
repo_track_justification: The public Git commit history (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/commits/main) records changes, authors, and timestamps.
repo_interim_justification: The repository exposes ongoing main commits (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/commits/main) and pull requests (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/pulls), not only final release archives.
repo_distributed_justification: README clone instructions (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md) use Git, a common distributed version-control system.
report_process_justification: SUPPORT (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/SUPPORT.md) directs users to the issue chooser (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues/new/choose) and specifies useful report content.
report_tracker_justification: Individual reports are tracked in GitHub issues (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues) with structured issue forms (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/tree/v0.1.0/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE).
report_responses_justification: The public issue archive (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues?q=is%3Aissue) returned zero open or closed issues on 2026-07-23; therefore no qualifying external bug report in the 2-12 month window is awaiting acknowledgement. Reviewer action: Maintainer must re-check the complete issue history immediately before submission. Limitation: This is a zero-report historical observation, not a promise, response-time target, or SLA.
enhancement_responses_justification: The public issue archive (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues?q=is%3Aissue) returned zero open or closed issues on 2026-07-23; therefore no qualifying external enhancement request in the 2-12 month window is awaiting a response. Reviewer action: Maintainer must re-check the complete issue history immediately before submission. Limitation: There is no response sample from which to infer future responsiveness; no SLA is promised.
report_archive_justification: Reports and responses are retained in the public, searchable, URL-addressable GitHub issue archive (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues?q=is%3Aissue).
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY policy (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/SECURITY.md) publishes scope, safe-research boundaries, report content, and the private channel.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY policy (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/SECURITY.md) directs reporters to GitHub private vulnerability reporting (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/security/advisories/new) over HTTPS. Reviewer action: Repository owner must confirm private vulnerability reporting remains enabled before submission. Limitation: The advisory inbox and setting are not public evidence; enabled state is owner-verified.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: The public issue archive (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/issues?q=is%3Aissue) returned zero issues on 2026-07-23, and the maintainer confirmed that GitHub contains no repository advisory/report. The official criterion permits N/A when no vulnerability report was received in the last six months. Reviewer action: Maintainer must re-check the public tracker and private advisory inbox immediately before submission; if a report appears, select Met only if every initial response was within 14 days. Limitation: This is a dated zero-report observation, and the policy deliberately promises no acknowledgement or remediation SLA.
build_justification: package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) defines pnpm build through Turborepo; the CI workflow (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the core verification lane including the build. Limitation: This assessment did not rerun the build; release owner must require a successful current-revision CI result.
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses common Node ecosystem tools: pnpm, Turborepo, Vite/vinext, TypeScript, and Civet as declared in package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) and README stack (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md).
build_floss_tools_justification: The documented pnpm build path in package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) uses repository/workspace dependencies and requires no proprietary build tool or service. Limitation: Optional hosted providers are runtime adapters, not required build tools.
test_justification: FLOSS Vitest and Playwright suites and their commands are public in package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json), tests (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/tree/v0.1.0/tests), and the testing guide (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/testing-and-evidence.md).
test_invocation_justification: package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) exposes the standard Node-ecosystem pnpm test command plus focused test:* commands.
test_most_justification: The checked-in coverage summary (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/assessments/coverage-summary.json) measures 70.29% lines and 62.35% branches (65.74% functions; 68.09% statements), which does not defensibly establish coverage of most branches, inputs, and functionality. Reviewer action: Test owner should raise meaningful branch and behavior coverage before reconsidering. Limitation: Coverage excludes integration/browser projects and selected timing-dependent modules as documented; those exclusions do not justify marking this criterion Met.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: CI workflow (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs automated core, coverage, integration, graph, and browser verification on pushes and pull requests. Reviewer action: Release owner must confirm the workflow file is on main and the target revision has a successful run. Limitation: A workflow definition is not itself proof of a particular run's conclusion.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONTRIBUTING.md) requires tests when observable behavior is created or modified; CONVENTIONS (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONVENTIONS.md) defines behavior-first testing.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major surfaces have paired behavior tests, including contact runtime tests (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/apps/web/src/app/api/orpc/%5B...rest%5D/contact-runtime.test.civet), auth boundary tests (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/auth/src/boundary.test.civet), and browser journeys (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/tree/v0.1.0/tests/e2e). Limitation: Examples establish current practice, not complete coverage; see test_most.
tests_documented_added_justification: The add/update-tests rule is explicit in CONTRIBUTING (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the expected test types are documented in CONVENTIONS (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CONVENTIONS.md).
warnings_justification: package.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) enables Biome/Ultracite lint, Markdown lint, strict TypeScript, and Civet typechecking; tsconfig.base.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/tsconfig.base.json) enables strict and additional safety flags. Limitation: Biome intentionally excludes authored .civet; Civet/TypeScript typechecking and tests cover that separate boundary.
warnings_fixed_justification: The core verification script (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/package.json) and CI workflow (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) make lint/typecheck failures blocking rather than advisory. Limitation: This review did not run the repository-wide lint/typecheck gates.
warnings_strict_justification: tsconfig.base.json (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/tsconfig.base.json) enables strict, exact optional types, unchecked-index protection, no implicit returns/override, and fallthrough checks; Biome config (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/biome.json) extends Ultracite with narrow documented exceptions. Limitation: skipLibCheck applies to dependency declarations and Biome does not parse Civet; this is strict within the supported tool boundaries, not literally every possible warning.
crypto_published_justification: Application-owned primitives use published algorithms through platform libraries: HMAC-SHA-256 in contact runtime (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/apps/web/src/app/api/orpc/%5B...rest%5D/contact-runtime.civet), SHA-256/HMAC and CSPRNGs in email preview (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/email/src/server/preview.civet), and Better Auth crypto in auth server (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/auth/src/server.civet). Limitation: Cloudflare/host TLS configuration is provider-owned and is not claimed as an application-implemented protocol.
crypto_call_justification: The application calls Web Crypto, Node crypto, and Better Auth in the cited contact runtime (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/apps/web/src/app/api/orpc/%5B...rest%5D/contact-runtime.civet), email preview (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/email/src/server/preview.civet), and auth server (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/auth/src/server.civet); it does not implement cryptographic algorithms itself.
crypto_floss_justification: The cryptographic functionality is implemented with the FLOSS Node/Web Crypto runtimes and pinned FLOSS Better Auth dependency recorded in pnpm lockfile (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/pnpm-lock.yaml). Limitation: Hosted TLS terminators may be used operationally, but no proprietary primitive is required to implement delivered functionality.
crypto_keylength_justification: Application-owned keyed HMAC paths accept a 32-byte/256-bit test binding and HMAC-SHA-256; production auth/contact secrets require at least 32 characters in .env.schema (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/.env.schema) and server config validation (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/config/src/server.civet). Reviewer action: Deployment owner must generate high-entropy secrets; length validation cannot prove entropy. Limitation: TLS negotiation and certificate key sizes belong to the deployment/provider, not DarkFactory's application-owned crypto.
crypto_working_justification: The application-owned defaults cited above use SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-256, Scrypt via Better Auth, Web Crypto/Node CSPRNGs, and no broken algorithm listed by the criterion. Reviewer action: Security reviewer should reconfirm the pinned Better Auth implementation at release. Limitation: This review does not attest to an operator's TLS cipher configuration.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The default application-owned primitives evidenced in contact runtime (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/apps/web/src/app/api/orpc/%5B...rest%5D/contact-runtime.civet), email preview (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/email/src/server/preview.civet), and auth server (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/auth/src/server.civet) do not use SHA-1, MD5, RC4, DES, or a custom cipher. Limitation: Provider TLS configuration remains outside the repository's direct control.
crypto_pfs_justification: DarkFactory does not implement a key-agreement protocol. HTTPS termination and forward-secrecy cipher selection are responsibilities of Cloudflare/the chosen deployment provider, while security guidance (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/security.md) requires HTTPS. Reviewer action: Deployment owner should configure modern provider TLS independently. Limitation: N/A is for application-owned key agreement; it is not a claim that every deployment has perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: auth server (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/auth/src/server.civet) delegates hashing and verification to pinned Better Auth 1.6.24 and stores only the returned hash; the resolved dependency uses Scrypt with a fresh 16-byte random salt per hash. Reviewer action: Security reviewer must reconfirm the pinned Better Auth password implementation/version at release. Limitation: The Scrypt parameters live in the dependency rather than repository-owned source; no plaintext-password storage claim extends to external operators or logs.
crypto_random_justification: Security-sensitive values use Node/Web Crypto CSPRNG APIs (randomBytes, randomUUID, and Better Auth's random salt) in email preview (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/email/src/server/preview.civet), API context (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/api/src/server/context.civet), and auth server (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/packages/auth/src/server.civet). Limitation: Random UUIDs used only as identifiers are included as supporting evidence, not treated as encryption keys.
delivery_mitm_justification: Source, clone, issues, and planned release delivery use HTTPS at the GitHub repository (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory); README clone instructions (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md) use the HTTPS Git URL. Reviewer action: Release owner must publish v0.1.0 through GitHub HTTPS. Limitation: No separate signed package is claimed.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The documented setup in README (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/README.md) uses HTTPS and a frozen pnpm lockfile (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/pnpm-lock.yaml); the repository does not instruct users to trust an unsigned checksum retrieved over HTTP. Limitation: This is a repository-instruction review, not a claim that every downstream mirror is secure.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The maintainer confirmed on 2026-07-23 that GitHub has no DarkFactory repository advisory and no matching NVD record; the same bounded result is recorded in the forthcoming 0.1.0 CHANGELOG Security section (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md). No unpatched medium-or-higher project vulnerability older than 60 days is therefore identified. Reviewer action: Security reviewer must repeat the repository-advisory and NVD check immediately before submission and reassess any new match. Limitation: This is a dated maintainer-confirmed advisory/NVD check, not a general vulnerability scan or claim that the software is vulnerability-free.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: The public issue archive contains zero reports, and the maintainer confirmed on 2026-07-23 that GitHub has no DarkFactory repository advisory; the bounded result is recorded in the forthcoming 0.1.0 CHANGELOG Security section (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md). Reviewer action: Maintainer must re-check public and private reporting channels before submission; if a critical report exists, assess its actual response time. Limitation: This zero-report observation is not a future response guarantee or SLA.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No DAST/web scanner or fuzzer is configured, and the coverage summary (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/assessments/coverage-summary.json) reports 62.35% branch coverage, below the official 80% automated-test-suite alternative. Reviewer action: Security/test owner must add and run a qualifying scanner/fuzzer or establish at least 80% branch coverage before changing this status. Limitation: The existing automated tests execute the software, but their measured branch coverage does not reach the criterion threshold.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The delivered authored implementation languages are Civet, TypeScript/JavaScript, SQL, and shell; it does not include authored C/C++ or another memory-unsafe implementation language requiring ASAN-style analysis. Reviewer action: Re-evaluate if native/memory-unsafe code is added. Limitation: Native transitive dependencies are not project-authored source for this criterion.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No documented test or fuzz configuration was established that enables many assertions for dynamic analysis; see the testing guide (https://github.com/jeffscottward/darkfactory/blob/v0.1.0/docs/testing-and-evidence.md). Reviewer action: Security/test owner must document and run a testing or fuzzing configuration that enables many assertions before changing this status. Limitation: Testing can qualify for this suggestion; the gap is the absence of an evidenced assertion-enabled configuration, not the use of tests itself.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No qualifying dynamic code analysis is run and therefore no vulnerability has been found through that channel; the official criterion expressly permits N/A in this case. Reviewer action: Re-evaluate every confirmed medium-or-higher finding if DAST/fuzzing is introduced. Limitation: N/A does not claim the application has no vulnerabilities.
